title: Artificial intelligence-assisted feedback in pharmacology education: a pilot evaluation of a custom generative model.
summary: Primary BMC Medical Education Methods/Results prospectively pilot a custom GPT-4-family model for pharmacology SAQ feedback. Among 20 students/80 answers, 12 outputs needed no edits, eight required amendments (four major); AI cut marking time 508 to 34 seconds per quiz. Human moderation was essential.
ai_technology: Custom GPT using a rubric and curated pharmacology references generates structured feedback; faculty review/moderation was part of intervention.
organization: Department of Medical Education; Royal Sussex County Hospital

evidence.tested: Prospective pilot reports generation time, faculty correction rates, blinded scoring of only five submissions, and student views from 11 respondents.
evidence.unknown: Faculty moderation and a very small blinded comparison provide only pilot-level accuracy evidence; major safety-relevant omissions occurred, no learning outcomes assessed.
evidence.ai_role: Custom GPT using a rubric and curated pharmacology references generates structured feedback; faculty review/moderation was part of intervention.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
